search_log: Searched “The Teeth of the Tiger” with Tom Clancy plus excerpt, first chapter, publisher, point of view, narrator, and third-person terms.
Opened and inspected the official Tom Clancy 23-page PDF and Penguin Random House’s sustained Chapter One excerpt; both consistently use third-person narration.

Searched specifically for first-person narration, epistolary form, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; no credible evidence of sustained base narration in another grammatical person was found.
Checked Google Books and Open Library results, but their catalog descriptions and preview metadata did not independently establish narrative person.
Excluded Wikisource and Project Gutenberg results because they concern Maurice Leblanc’s different novel with the same title.
person_note: The controlling voice is a nonparticipating third-person narrator that shifts focalization among several characters and sometimes renders their thoughts. The interior quote sequence concerning Mohammed matches the externally attributed thought technique in the authorized opening excerpts. First-person forms occur only in dialogue, while the visible “you” forms are generic maxims or conversational address, so neither supports first- or second-person base narration. Multiple focal characters and plot strands remain third person rather than constituting person alternation. The main limitation is that the authorized prose samples cover the opening rather than the entire book, but the interior Goodreads evidence and explicit whole-book description corroborate them, with no credible contrary structure found.
